findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key, so the assertion fails
findings.body: In test_dedupe, the expected IssueOccurrence is constructed with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH), which embeds the fingerprint ['<detector_id>:val1'] via handler.build_fingerprint("val1"). However, evaluate_group_key_value is then invoked with group_key "group_key", so the occurrence the handler actually produces carries fingerprint ['<detector_id>:group_key']. DetectorEvaluationResult and IssueOccurrence are both frozen dataclasses whose equality compares every field (unlike StatusChangeMessage, IssueOccurrence.__eq__ is not patched in these tests), so the final `assert handler.evaluate_group_key_value(...) == expected_result` compares occurrences with different fingerprints and fails. The expected occurrence should be built with group_key "group_key" to match the key passed to evaluate_group_key_value.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and will raise TypeError when instantiated via Detector.detector_handler
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from a concrete DetectorHandler subclass (with an evaluate that returned []) to a StatefulDetectorHandler subclass with an empty body. StatefulDetectorHandler still has unimplemented abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Because DetectorHandler inherits abc.ABC, calling MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector) raises TypeError ("Can't instantiate abstract class ... with abstract methods ..."). MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points at this class, and Detector.detector_handler executes group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector of type metric_alert_fire that flows through process_detectors will now crash instead of simply producing no results as before. Either provide stub implementations of the abstract methods or keep the class on DetectorHandler until the real stateful implementation lands. (The TODO comment above the class saying "This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" is also now stale, since it already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.)

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still documents a list return type
findings.body: The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but this PR changed both this method and the abstract DetectorHandler.evaluate to return a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey (dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]). The stale wording misleads anyone implementing the abstract method or consuming the results; it should describe the dict keyed by group key.
